entry.title: Two Journeys
entry.content:
One should walk outside,
but also walk within.

Outside, everything is separate;
inside, everything is One.

Outside, trees stay silent;
inside, they whisper tales.

Outside, foreign trips cost a fortune;
inside, foreign trips are free — and far more real.

The souvenirs you bring from outside may break or be lost,
but the ones brought from inside will stay forever.

— Asim Zulfiqar
entry.summary: One should walk outside, but also walk within.

entry.title: Poem: Time - Money or resource ?
entry.content:
On an unusual day,
while wandering inside myself,
I saw Time — sitting on the side.

In wonder I asked,
“Why the long face?”
“I am tired of my names,” it said.

“What? What names?”
“Money, resource, thief — and what not?
People think what I am not,
and abuse me with verbs.”

“Verbs like invest, spend, waste —
which I do not understand.”

“Then who are you? Tell us.”
“I am me — I have my own identity.

I cannot be spent,
I cannot be wasted,
I cannot be invested like money.

I don’t have an explanation in words,
but you can consider me as your friend.

A friend with whom you sit
without any expectation,
a friend with whom you sip your tea.

If you will sit with me,
I will stay with you.
All the moments you lived
could be brought back.”

I will take you to unexplored worlds,
worlds of wonder —
where you might find yourself.

I nodded —
“I see your point,
but I need to go now.
I have another meeting scheduled at four.

I’ll meet you some other day,
maybe when I will have time.”

— Asim Zulfiqar
(Inspired from the book Metaphors we live by - Book by George Lakoff and Mark Johnson)
entry.summary: On an unusual day, while wandering inside myself, I saw Time — sitting on the side.

entry.title: Poem: لفظوں کی قیمت (The Cost of Words)

link.title: Poem: لفظوں کی قیمت (The Cost of Words)

entry.content:
لفظ جو تم منہ سے کہہ دیتے ہو
(Lafz jo tum muh se keh dete ho)
The words that you utter from your mouth,

روح اسکی کھو دیتے ہو
(Rooh uski kho dete ho)
You lose their soul.

دل میں جو ایک گھر بنایا ہوتا ہے
(Dil mein jo ik ghar bnaya hota hai)
The home that was built in the heart,

ایک لفظ سے اسے گرا دیتے ہو
(Ik lafz se use gira dete ho)
You demolish it with a single word.

خاموشی سے ملتی ہے، اس گھر کو سکونت
(Khamoshi se milti hai, us ghar ko sakoonat)
Silence brings peace to that home,

لفظوں سے وہ لڑکھڑا جاتا ہے
(Lafzon se wo ladkhada jata hai)
Words make it stumble.

بولو تبھی جب ضرورت ہو
(Bolo tabhi jab zarorat ho)
Speak only when there is need.

ہر لفظ تم سے تمہارا کچھ لے جاتا ہے
(Har lafz tum se tumhara kuch le jata hai)
Every word takes something of yours away from you.

— Asim Zulfiqar
(Originally written in Urdu)

entry.title: Poem: The Smoke’s Journey
entry.content:
How about,
on a sunny day,
on a beach,
I smoked a cigarette full of weed.

As I smoked,
the smoke rose up,
drifted here and there,
and slowly went inside me.

As I watched it dissolve,
I became a particle of smoke
and went inside myself.

As I descended,
I saw colonies,
colors,
and fire.

Colonies of cells, viruses, germs, and bacteria.
Colors — almost like rainbows and flowers —
formed by the movement of neurons and blood.
Fire — of war, anger, and jealousy.

As I went deeper into the bacterial colonies,
I saw them talking.
They were using “I, you, we, us, me” — just like we do.
They were arguing,
claiming land,
defending their space.

Then I moved to the land of cells.
They were busy fighting the viruses,
falling one by one,
but still fighting for their resources.

I peeked into the colony of viruses.
They had their reason too.
They just wanted to exist,
to let their offspring grow.

Even the germs —
were on strike.

And then I started to ascend,
because I was smoke,
and smoke never stays long.

I was released from my body
and became me again.

As I became conscious,
I wondered —
if they all live inside me,
and fight like we do,
then maybe we too
are living inside something bigger,
laughing,
arguing,
and calling it life.

— Asim Zulfiqar
entry.summary: How about, on a sunny day, on a beach, I smoked a cigarette full of weed.

entry.title: Poem: تُو ہمیشہ مُڑ سکدا (You Can Always Turn Back)

link.title: Poem: تُو ہمیشہ مُڑ سکدا (You Can Always Turn Back)

entry.content:
دودھ جیہڑا لسی بن جاوے
(Dodh jehra lassi ban jāve)
Milk that becomes lassi, او مُڑ کے دودھ بندا نئیں
(O mur ke dodh ban da nahī̃)
Cannot turn back into milk.

سرسوں جیہڑی ساگ بن جاوے
(Sarso jehrī sāg ban jāve)
Mustard that becomes saag, او مُڑ کے سرسوں بندی نئیں
(Oh mur ke sarso bandī nahī̃)
Cannot turn back into mustard.

آم جیہڑا اچار ہو جاوے
(Aam jehrā achār ho jāve)
Mango that becomes pickle, او مُڑ کے آم نہیں بندا
(Oh mur ke aam nahī̃ ban da)
Cannot turn back into mango.

پر اوہ عاصم، جے تُو لسی وی بن جاوے
(Par oh Asim, je tū̃ lassi vī ban jāve)
But O Asim, even if you become lassi, تُو مُڑ کے کھیر بن سکدا
(Tū mur ke khīr ban sakdā)
You can still become kheer.

تُو ساگ بن کے وی
(Tū sāg ban ke vī)
Even becoming saag, سرسوں وانگ کھِل سکدا
(Sarso vāṅg khil sakdā)
You can bloom like mustard.

تُو اچار ورگا کھٹّا ہو کے وی
(Tū achār warga khaṭṭā hoke vī)
Even sour like pickle, واپس آم ورگا مِٹھا ہو سکدا
(Wāpis ām warga miṭhā ho sakdā)
You can become sweet like mango again.

تُو ہمیشہ مُڑ سکدا
(Tū hameshā mur sakdā)
You can always turn back, جے دل چ تیرے چاہ ہووے
(Je dil ch tere chāh hove)
If there is desire in your heart.

— Asim Zulfiqar
(Originally written in Punjabi)
